name: Multi-well correlation via relative geologic time and loop consistency: Sylvester 2023 ChronoLog (pairwise DTW + least-squares RGT), Wheeler & Hale 2014 simultaneous correlation, incremental/hierarchical multi-well correlation (2018, 2025), and the in-competition analogue (ROGII 3rd place sibling-lateral reference GR)
authors_org: Zoltan Sylvester (Bureau of Economic Geology, UT Austin); Loralee Wheeler and Dave Hale (Colorado School of Mines); incremental correlation following geologically optimal neighbours (Edwards, Lallier, Caumon et al., RING/Universite de Lorraine [uncertain]); 'On the Influence of the Correlation Path in Incremental Multi-well Stratigraphic Correlation' (Springer, 2025, RING group [uncertain]); ROGII 3rd-place team (local writeup 3rd.txt).
year: 2014 (Wheeler & Hale), 2018 (incremental correlation), 2022 (Sylvester EarthArXiv preprint), 2023 (Sylvester, Basin Research 35:1961), 2025 (correlation-path paper; ROGII competition)
venue_link: Sylvester 2023, 'Automated multi-well stratigraphic correlation and model building using relative geologic time', Basin Research https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1111/bre.12787 (preprint https://eartharxiv.org/repository/view/3508/); Wheeler & Hale 2014, 'Simultaneous correlation of multiple well logs', SEG Expanded Abstracts 618-622 https://onepetro.org/SEGAM/proceedings-pdf/SEG14/All-SEG14/SEG-2014-0227/1513284/seg-2014-0227.pdf ; incremental correlation https://www.researchgate.net/publication/325604900 ; correlation path 2025 https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-031-92870-3_5 ; ROGII 3rd place writeup (local C:/Users/Aadinarayan R/Desktop/CSE/projects/Erudition/3rd.txt); 1st place XY-neighbour section (local 1st.txt); 2nd place 'explicit formation modeling' rejection (local 2nd.txt)
code_availability: Sylvester: data and notebooks at https://github.com/zsylvester/chronolog_data; ChronoLog package referenced on https://zsylvester.github.io/research/ (public repo location not confirmed) [uncertain]. Wheeler & Hale: Mines JTK (Java) implementation, not packaged [uncertain]. ROGII 3rd place: code linked from their writeup (Kaggle notebook).
evidence_level: Sylvester and Wheeler & Hale: peer-reviewed (abstract/preprint summary read; full text 403). Incremental correlation: peer-reviewed (snippet only). ROGII 3rd place: competition writeup with private-LB ablations (read in full locally).
extreme_summary: Instead of correlating each well to one reference, run many pairwise DTW correlations between neighbouring wells (e.g. over a triangulated well graph), then solve one global least-squares problem for a per-well depth-to-RGT shift so all pairwise ties are satisfied jointly; this closes loops and removes the path dependence of chained DTW. In ROGII, the working version of 'use the neighbours' was not an XY surface prior but using sibling laterals' GR binned in TVT as additional reference curves, which gave the 3rd place team their largest private-LB gains (-0.10 to -0.13 ft).
task_definition: Classical: assign every depth sample in every well a relative geologic time (chronostratigraphic position) so that correlative layers share the same RGT across the basin. For ROGII (our reading): predict TVT along a lateral, where TVT against a typewell is exactly an RGT coordinate; labelled training laterals near or sharing a typewell with the target provide extra GR(TVT) references and extra structural constraints.
inputs: Classical: GR (or other) logs of hundreds of vertical wells plus their map locations. ROGII 3rd place: target lateral GR, its typewell GR, and GR of training laterals sharing the same typewell (siblings), binned by their known TVT; optionally distance-weighted by XY.
target_parameterisation: Relative geologic time per sample (monotone in depth for vertical wells); per-well shift function depth -> RGT. For laterals, TVT (or u = TVT + Z in structural coordinates) plays the role of RGT and is not monotone in MD.
output_representation: Classical: a single consistent RGT field (point estimate) plus chronostratigraphic (Wheeler) diagram and 3D model. 3rd place: HMM/PF posterior mean paths using a mixture of references.
architecture: Sylvester/ChronoLog: (1) choose well pairs from a neighbour graph (Delaunay triangulation of well locations [uncertain]); (2) pairwise DTW on normalised logs for every edge; (3) convert each DTW path into equations 'shift_i(z_a) - shift_j(z_b) = z_a - z_b style' constraints and solve the sparse least-squares system for all per-well RGT shifts with conjugate gradients (Wheeler & Hale variant); (4) flatten logs into RGT, multi-scale blocking with continuous wavelet transform to propagate boundaries and build a 3D model. Incremental methods instead add wells one at a time along a geologically optimal path, guaranteeing non-crossing layers. ROGII 3rd place: HMM whose hidden state includes TVT position, formation rate d(TVT+Z)/dMD, GR bias, and reference family (typewell-oriented vs sibling-oriented reference curve, weights 0.2/0.8), plus a self-reference built from the target's own known prefix; PF with the same references; fine-bin (0.0625 ft) sibling HMM; distance-weighted sibling HMM variant.
core_mechanism: Consistency through joint optimisation: each pairwise correlation is noisy and may lock onto a wrong repeated cycle, but a wrong tie cannot be satisfied around every loop of the well graph, so the least-squares solution down-weights it (loop closure). In ROGII terms, a sibling lateral that crossed the same interval gives an independent, calibrated GR(TVT) sample of the same stratigraphy acquired with lateral-tool characteristics, so the band ambiguity of the typewell (which may be a different vintage/tool) is reduced, and several references vote on the band.
training_objective: No learning: DTW cost (squared/abs log difference) per pair, then an L2 least-squares misfit over all pairwise ties with smoothness regularisation. 3rd place HMM: Student-t (nu=1) GR emission, smooth transitions, forward-backward posterior mean.
decoding: Least-squares solution (L2 -> mean-like); 3rd place: forward-backward posterior mean (RMSE-consistent).
metric_consistent_decode: Yes for the least-squares RGT (mean under Gaussian residuals) and for the 3rd place posterior mean. Pairwise DTW itself is mode-seeking (single best path); the global L2 averaging partly corrects that.
evidence_scope: Multiple wells jointly (whole basin for ChronoLog; target + siblings + typewell for 3rd place).
prefix_conditioning: Classical: none. 3rd place: known prefix used as self-reference GR template and as clamped HMM states (last 128 rows prepended, initial rate from last 256 rows).
propose_vs_select: Single consistent solution. As used in ROGII, sibling-reference trackers are separate candidate trajectories fed to a SoftMax gate, i.e. usable as ensemble members or as extra channels.
physical_constraints: Monotone RGT in each vertical well (no layer crossing), loop closure across the well graph, smooth shifts; 3rd place: rate caps (|rate| <= 0.25, integrated correction <= 10 ft), smooth dip state.
dataset: Sylvester: close to 700 wells, Permian Basin (Spraberry Formation, West Texas), maps subtle channel bodies. Wheeler & Hale: tens of Teapot Dome/other vertical wells [uncertain]. ROGII: 773 training laterals whose typewells consolidate into 54 master systems (our seq_NN_master_typewell.py), 155-well internal holdout in Erudition.
synthetic_to_real: Not applicable for the classical methods (real logs, no learning). For Erudition, sibling-reference channels exist only for real wells; synthetic wells would need synthetic siblings (the master-typewell simulator can generate several laterals through one master system) or the channel set to a neutral value, with the risk that the network learns to ignore it (85% synthetic).
metric_and_performance: Sylvester: qualitative, correlations robust enough to map subtle stratigraphic detail previously thought feasible only manually; no RMSE vs manual tops in the abstract [uncertain]. Wheeler & Hale: globally optimal alignment, insensitive to large measurement errors (qualitative). ROGII 3rd place (private LB, ft RMSE): spatial-distance-weighted sibling HMM 5.817 -> 5.691 (-0.126); rational distance weighting 5.817 -> 5.720 (-0.097); HMM mixture OOF 6.049 -> 5.970 when adding Local-DTW and fine-bin sibling HMM families; fold-specific reference pools 5.726 -> 5.718. 1st place XY neighbour channels (surface S = TVT + Z + C, locally linear, fitted by weighted LS over XY neighbours): improved CV by ~0.3 but hurt public LB; standalone 11.4 CV / 12.9 LB. 2nd place: explicit formation surfaces from neighbours captured coarse topography but did not fix bad wells.
comparability: 3rd place numbers are pooled RMSE in ft on the ROGII private LB (directly comparable in units, not in wells or baseline strength; their base was an HMM ~5.8, weaker than our 4.84 ft single model on our holdout). Classical RGT papers are not quantitatively comparable.
validation_protocol: 3rd place reports private-LB deltas across solution branches (not identical pipelines) and uses fold-specific reference pools to avoid leakage; GroupKFold by well. Sibling features are leakage-prone: a holdout well must only see siblings from the training fold, and siblings must never include itself.
inference_budget: Pairwise DTW over a few siblings plus a small least-squares solve: well under a second per well on CPU. Building binned sibling reference curves: milliseconds. Fits Kaggle and rig budgets.
repeated_layers: This is the main attraction. Band confusion arises because the typewell GR has self-similar cycles; a sibling lateral that drilled the same interval provides GR(TVT) with the same tool response and local thickness, so its signature at the candidate bands can differ where the typewell's does not (thickness changes, local facies). Loop consistency further rejects a band choice that disagrees with multiple neighbours. 3rd place keeps reference families as separate hidden states rather than averaging, preserving multimodality until evidence resolves it.
drift: Partly. Siblings constrain local structure (dip) near the target only if they are laterally close; the XY-surface route (1st place, our failed geo prior) attacked drift directly but failed at the leaderboard, probably due to label inconsistency between interpreters. Distance-weighted siblings give an implicit local dip prior without imposing an explicit surface.
uncertainty_and_calibration: Classical least squares gives no calibrated uncertainty (residual misfit per tie can flag unreliable wells). Incremental/stochastic correlation literature (RING) samples multiple consistent correlations for uncertainty. 3rd place uses PF multimodality and reference-family posteriors as gate features, no calibration analysis.
where_to_use: (1) New cost-image channels built from sibling laterals: for each target, collect training-fold laterals whose typewell belongs to the same master system (seq_NN_master_typewell.py already finds the 54 systems), bin their GR by labelled TVT into a sibling reference curve sib_gr(TVT) on the 400-level grid (optionally inverse-distance weighted by XY), and add 'sib_gr' and '|gr - sib_gr|' (and a sibling-count/coverage mask) as channels alongside tw_gr and gr_abs_diff. (2) Consistency-based reranking of humps: for multimodal columns, score each significant hump by GR match against several independent references (typewell, siblings, self-prefix) instead of the XY-surface position the failed geo prior used. (3) A cheap 3rd-place-style sibling-reference HMM/DP as a diverse ensemble or gate member.
error_mode_targeted: Band confusion (~51%: wrong_mode 24%, blend 15%, multimodal_miss 12%) primarily; drift (~25%) secondarily via local structural agreement.
gap_vs_our_implementation: Erudition uses exactly one reference curve per well: the provided typewell (channels tw_gr, gr_abs_diff, tw_tvt_rel). The only multi-well information tried is the XY geo prior (geo_tvt_diff and related channels, commented out in unet_static_channels; posterior_geo_pick.py hump picking), which models neighbours as a structural surface S = TVT + Z + C -- the one form of neighbour use that failed on the Kaggle LB for 1st place and failed in our own experiment (geo-nearest hump = truth only 52.4% vs dominant hump 76.2%, chance 46.2%). What we do not do: (a) use neighbour/sibling wells' GR as additional reference signals (grep for 'sibling' in the solution tree finds nothing); (b) use the target's own known prefix GR vs its labelled TVT as a self-reference channel (3rd place found it useful because GR calibration is shared between prefix and suffix); (c) enforce any cross-well consistency of band choice. The master-typewell consolidation already exists but is used only for synthetic generation, not for building reference channels.
proposed_experiment: E0 (diagnostic, CPU, no retraining, uses existing dump results/baseline_check_posterior_all): for each holdout well, build sib_gr(TVT) from training-fold siblings in the same master system (fold-safe; exclude holdout wells), and a self-prefix reference from the well's own known section. On multimodal columns, pick the significant hump whose GR match (mean |gr - ref| over the column's 32 ft window) is best under sib_gr, and under typewell for comparison; report truth-hump hit rate vs the dominant hump's 76.2% and the geo prior's 52.4%, plus a split-half-tuned soft reweight p'(x) ~ p(x) * exp(-match(x)/T) like posterior_geo_pick.py's geo_reweight. Also report sibling coverage (fraction of holdout wells and TVT levels with >= 1 sibling). Stop if the hit rate is not clearly above 76.2% on covered columns. E1 (if E0 positive): in experiments/bilzard/seq_NN_dataset.py compute channels sib_gr, sib_gr_abs_diff, sib_count (and self_prefix_gr, self_prefix_abs_diff); for synthetic wells, generate 1-3 synthetic siblings from the same master series via the existing Simulator so the channel is populated in training; register channels in seq_NN_cfg.py (16 -> 19-21 channels). 60-epoch ConvNeXt vs control 5.47 ft, 2 seeds; success > 0.39 ft; then 150 epochs and FastViT KD. E2 (optional): a ChronoLog-style least-squares consistency step -- pairwise DTW between the target's predicted GR(TVT) profile and each sibling's, solve for a per-well TVT shift minimising all ties, apply as a closed-form offset correction to the expectation decode; test on the dump only.
implementation_effort: Low for E0 (~150 lines numpy on existing dumps plus master-system grouping). Medium for E1 (channel building in dataset, fold-safe sibling pools, synthetic siblings). Medium-high for a full RGT least-squares solver (E2).
gpu_cost: E0 and E2: CPU only. E1: same as a baseline 60/150-epoch run on RTX 5060 8 GB (+3-5 input channels, negligible compute).
distillation_compatibility: Compatible: new inputs are available to the FastViT student; E2 is a post-hoc correction on any model's output.
error_correlation_with_ours: Channels inside the same net: correlated errors, gains via new evidence. A sibling-reference HMM/DP tracker (3rd place style) would have substantially different errors from ConvNeXt/FastViT (different evidence and inductive bias), making it a good gate/blend member -- though our learned per-point gates have failed before, so a simple well-level blend is safer.
risk: (1) Coverage: holdout wells whose master system has few or no training siblings get nothing; 54 systems for 773 wells suggests good coverage on average but uneven [uncertain]. (2) Leakage: siblings' labels must come only from training folds; the Kaggle test set also had siblings in train, but our internal holdout must mimic that exactly. (3) Label inconsistency across interpreters (1st place's explanation for XY failure) also affects sibling TVT labels, blurring sib_gr. (4) Siblings may have drilled a different TVT range, leaving sib_gr undefined at the confused bands. (5) The 85% synthetic training mix may teach the net to ignore the channel unless synthetic siblings are realistic. (6) Classical RGT methods assume monotone vertical logs; laterals revisit levels non-monotonically, so ChronoLog cannot be applied as-is, only its consistency principle.
notes: Strongest evidence is in-competition: 3rd place called reference-GR design 'the most important HMM decision' and the source of their largest private gains (sibling-lateral GR, fine TVT bins, self-prefix reference, keeping reference families separate). 2nd place's rejection of explicit formation modelling and 1st place's XY LB degradation agree with our failed geo prior: neighbours help as GR references, not as structural surfaces. Overlaps A03 (DTW), A15 (structural coordinate u = TVT + Z), A18 (TVT + Z - ANCC identity), B07 (seismic RGT). Deep-learning multi-well correlators (DHGC CNN+DP 2026, KANFormer, ASDNet) remain vertical-well and single-pair; none implement loop consistency end-to-end.
